title: The ninety-nine, all of them
hookLine: the ninety-nine names, counted on beads or on fingertips, one a day from here
tomorrow: box one of ninety-nine is empty. which name goes in it?

cards: A string of beads slipping through someone's fingers in the back seat of a car, at a bus stop, in a hospital waiting room. The sound is soft and steady, and what's being counted is the answer to yesterday's question.

The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said, in a report Bukhari and Muslim both record, in paraphrase: Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and whoever counts them and keeps them enters the Garden.
From tomorrow, this block meets them, one a day.

teach.b: The beads have a name, misbaha, and people loop them through their fingers saying subhanallah, glory be to Allah, or the names themselves. But here's the detail to tell a friend tonight.
Abu Dawud records a companion who saw the Prophet counting his glorifications on his own hand.

teach.h: FINGERTIPS WILL BE MADE TO SPEAK.
teach.b: And a woman named Yusayrah reports, in Tirmidhi's collection, that he told the women to count on their fingertips, because the fingertips will be asked, and made to speak. So in these reports, the counting tool is a hand.
Feel the joints of your fingers with your thumb: there's a counter you always carry. Then the number.
The hadith gives ninety-nine with a promise, but doesn't list them; the familiar list comes from a report in Tirmidhi's collection.

And a du'a in Ahmad's Musnad asks Allah by every name He has, even names He kept to Himself. So ninety-nine isn't a fence around Him. The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's words: Allah's are the fairest names.
Invoke Him by them. From here, a name a day, each one opened like a door.

how: Muslims count glorifications and the names of Allah on prayer beads (misbaha or subha) or on the joints of the fingers, often after the daily prayers.

o: a string of beads used for prayer, ninety-nine long
Allah's beautiful names, counted one at a time
the prophets named, one by one, in the Qur'an

games.q: counting the names — tap the pairs.

s: ninety-nine come with a promise; a du'a in Ahmad's Musnad asks by every name, even ones kept hidden.
in one report, the Prophet counted on his own hand
Abu Dawud records a companion who saw him counting his glorifications on his hand.
you need prayer beads to count the names
the reports point to fingertips, which will be asked and made to speak.

games.q: a friend got prayer beads as a gift and feels awkward: 'I don't know any of the ninety-nine. should I wait till I've learned them?' what fits today?
o: start with one name, on fingers or beads; the counting is how it begins.
wait until you've memorized all ninety-nine, then begin counting.
the beads are decoration; the names don't need counting at all.
games.why: the hadith's promise is for whoever counts the names and keeps them. one name, counted on the fingers, is where it begins.

practice: On a page, write the numbers one to ninety-nine in a grid, small, ten to a row. Go slowly and feel the pen move, a number for each breath if you like. If the sit ends before ninety-nine, that's fine; box one is for tomorrow's name.

wordCard.voice: The ninety-nine: the beautiful names of Allah, counted on beads or on fingertips, one door at a time.

orig.note: Arabic: the most beautiful names, the Qur'an's own phrase for them.

carryVoice: Keep this one: every name a door, and a whole hallway of them ahead. Talk soon.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 7392; Sahih Muslim 2677 (Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever counts them enters the Garden)
Sunan Abi Dawud 1502 (Abdullah ibn Amr: he saw the Prophet counting tasbih on his hand)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3583; Sunan Abi Dawud 1501 (Yusayrah: count on your fingertips, for they will be questioned and made to speak)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 3507 (the familiar list); Musnad Ahmad 3712 (the du'a asking by every name, including those kept in the unseen)

sources.q: Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them.
